title: For a son taken at dawn

plan.english: Boy, they seized you in the morning. Then they drove you away with the sheep. Here your cup is dry. Dear one, I seek you in the fields. I asked the shepherds, and they are silent. Who will lead you home to me? May I see you again, beloved!

plan.english: Here at the fence the men fell. Then with spears they protected our herd. The slayers were indeed many. Our dead lie on the earth. And now we women are mournful. May their fame be imperishable! Woman, now sing their names. May the people indeed remember them.

plan.english: Stones, grind the grain. I grind for my master; my hands have grown tired. My grandmother indeed ground by the spring. There I sang with my sisters. Here I sing alone. Grind, stone; now the night is long.

plan.english: I did carry gold to the king. Then I offered him silver and cows. He did not take my gifts; he laughed and turned away. My daughter weaves in his house. Now I carry the gold back. Father Sky, look at my grief!

plan.english: My cows are gone from the stall. The calves are hungry, and there is no milk. Now my grandsons suffer. And the hostile ones drink our milk. And they eat the flesh of our bulls. Perkunos, strike them with a stone!

plan.english: Now I sit by the sea and look toward the dawn. There my sister waits for me. My wife is sad indeed at the hearth. I was a free man; I am a servant. Wind, carry my word across the sea.

plan.english: In the autumn enemies came from the mountains. The dogs became restless, and the women woke. Then the warriors ran out with spears. The hostile ones killed them there and drove off the cattle. They carried off the women and the young ones and burned the settlement. One old woman hid in the cow-stall. She saw this, and she told it to us.

title: The grandmother who sought the boy

plan.english: Warriors carried off a shepherd's grandson at the river. His grandmother sought him for nine days. Then she arrived at their settlement. At the door she saw her grandson carrying water. She gave the master her silver. The master took it and let the boy go. Grandmother and grandson returned home, and she shed tears with joy.

title: The boy on the swift horse

plan.english: Other men captured a king's grandson. For three years he took care of their cattle. In the evenings he looked toward the dawn. Then he took a swift horse and fled in the night. His masters followed him. It was swifter than their horses. In the morning he came home unharmed. His grandfather saw him and shed tears.

plan.english: Warriors carried off a shepherd's young daughter. She ground their grain and wove wool. She grew old in their settlement. She nourished her master's grandsons. The master's boy asked her: Where is your village? She said: I do not remember its name. At night she was sad, and she sang the songs of her village.

title: The king who would not take the ransom

plan.english: A king seized the daughter of an old man. The old one brought him gold and silver. The king did not take them, and he drove the old one away. The old one sat down by the sea and called upon Sky. Sky heard him. For nine days a plague killed warriors and cattle. Then the king let the daughter go and gave gifts to the old one.

Sky heard him.

Then the king let the daughter go and gave gifts to the old one.

plan.english: Other men drove our cattle across the river. That night they ate up our oxen and drank the mead. We lay in the grass and heard their boast. Their king said: We are bolder than these herdsmen. Their women will grind our grain. We did not tremble. We grasped our spears and waited for the dawn. At dawn we seized our livestock.

We are bolder than these herdsmen.

We did not tremble.
We grasped our spears and waited for the dawn.
At dawn we seized our livestock.

title: The brother who found his sister

plan.english: Hostile men carried off a young girl and sold her to men of the sea. Her brother sought her for three years. Then he came to a far house. There a captive woman poured mead for the warriors. He recognized his own sister. He paid the master her ransom, and they returned home.

clauses.english: Hostile men carried off a young girl and sold her to men of the sea.

He recognized his own sister.
He paid the master her ransom, and they returned home.

plan.english: Enemy, may your cows die. And may it not rain on your fields. May your house burn in the darkness. And may your calves not grow up. May no one praise your name. And may dogs and birds eat you.

plan.english: Fence, guard my cattle at night. Dogs, be awake in the darkness. And may the slayer not find the path. And may his horse throw him. Perkunos, strike him with a stone. May my cows come to the stall in the evening.

plan.english: Dawn, daughter of Sky, hear me now. My daughter is a captive among others. Now shine for her and show the path. Free her, and lead her to me. I will give you milk and honey.

title: Curse on the one who refused the ransom

plan.english: You did not take my gold; you laughed, and I suffered. And may your daughter be a captive. May she then grind grain for others. May you indeed seek her and not find her. And may your wealth not save you.

plan.english: Nights, cover me with shadow. Dogs, be silent at the door. May my masters sleep. Path, now lead me toward the dawn. River, carry me; may I arrive at my hearth.

plan.english: Slayer, you killed our warriors at the fence. Their widows are wretched. Slayer, may your spear break. May the horses flee from you. May you die alone in the darkness. May no one lay you in the earth. Slayer, may your name now be lost.
